newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Fergie tells of her royal humiliation.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Fergie tells of her royal humiliation.

text.p: The Duchess of York on Tuesday described her humiliation in front of Britain's royal family and servants when pictures of her cavorting topless with her "financial adviser" were splashed across newspapers.

The Duchess, popularly known as Fergie, was holidaying with the royal family in Scotland when the damning pictures of her antics with Texan John Bryan at a villa in the south of France hit the front pages in 1992.
In an autobiography to be published next week, she describes entering the room for dinner to find everyone staring at her.
"I knew they must be seeing me topless being nuzzled by a bald American," she said in extracts published in Hello! magazine.

The papers carried page after page of the pictures of Fergie (Sarah Ferguson) and Bryan playing, kissing and apparently toe-sucking, in front of her two small daughters, Princesses Eugenie and Beatrice.
Her estranged husband, Queen Elizabeth's second son Prince Andrew, and his family had seen the pictures that morning as they sat round the breakfast table.
"It would be accurate to report that the porridge was getting cold. Eyes wide and mouths ajar, the adults were flipping through the Daily Mirror and the rest of the tabloids," Fergie said.
Although she was already separated from Prince Andrew the pictures were confirmation for the newspapers of the brash, self-centred ways that made the Duchess unfit to be a royal.
Fergie humbly agrees with them. "I had been exposed for what I truly was. Worthless. Unfit. A national disgrace," she says in the book, ghostwritten by American author Jeff Coplon.
A country girl from a broken home, Fergie says she was never cut out for royal life.
On her first meeting with the royal family, she tripped over a piano leg spilling her drink and then accidentally kicked one of the queen's corgi dogs as she tried to curtsey.
"It was a glancing blow, but corgis are a melodramatic breed and you would have thought the little yapper was bound for the royal kennel in the sky," she said.
It was characteristic of the blunders that would turn Fergie, in the eyes of the newspapers, from "a breath of fresh air" into a figure of ridicule.
But for all her candour and penitence, the Duchess believes that royal insiders, rather than her own behaviour, were responsible for her fall from grace.
"I could have looked like Michelle Pfeiffer, dressed like Jackie Onassis, and behaved like Mother Teresa, and at the end of the day it would have made no difference," she said.

She repeatedly describes the qualities she admired in her ex-husband and says how much she loved him, hinting that they were forced apart by royal mandarins. She and Andrew divorced earlier this year.
"In my opinion, the press is still missing that story today. As yet unwritten is the tale of how some of the most trusted people at Buckingham Palace have undermined the monarchy itself."

Fergie, who is reported to have huge debts, is said to have been paid 800,000 pounds ($1.3 million) for the autobiography and Hello! magazine is said to have paid a six-figure sum to publish the extracts.
